newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee ends broadly higher as roasters return.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee ends broadly higher as roasters return.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures, plagued by ongoing supply worries, sailed to a broadly higher close on Wednesday.

Benchmark July futures rose 5.05 cents a lb on the day, to 193.40, having traded from 185.50 to 196 cents. Spot May gained 3.10, to finish at 214.30, while the outer months gained between 0.05 and 5.00 cents.

News that negotiations aimed at resolving a truckers' strike in Colombia had reached a stalemate provided some impetus, but traders said the reappearance of steady roaster buying was even more significant today.
"You had a pretty broad base of roaster interest underneath," a New York-based trader said. "And everything gets magnified by a lack of origin selling overhead."
Traders said signs a recent round of speculative profit-taking had run its course spurred the early buying.
Once the trade buying set in, speculators were quick to follow, driving prices up by more than seven cents per lb at one point.
Light liquidation by commission houses and locals shaved a few cents off the rally, but the market settled into a broadly firmer range for the remainder of the session.

Overall turnover remained low for the third straight day, however, as coffee's unpredictable performance appeared to drive many operators to the sidelines. The day's volume was estimated at 7,232 lots.
Traders continued to keep a close eye on the situtation in Colombia, where truck drivers have been on strike since Saturday.
With arabica inventories already near historically low levels in the U.S., a prolonged work stoppage in Colombia, the world's number-two grower, could drive futures prices to new highs, they said.
"With the big premium out there on the spot contract, and a lack of deliverable coffee, I don't see any reason why this can't continue to go higher," the trader said.

Much of the day's volume was concentrated on the nearby switch, which narrowed substantially late in the session as speculators unloaded positions on the deliverable May contract. May's premium to July closed at 20.90, down from 22.85 cents on Tuesday.
Technically, July faced crucial hurdles at today's top of 196, followed by 199, a contract high set on Monday. To the downside, support was noted at 192.20, and then at 190 and 185.50 cents.
